notes.D3-05: FIX DEFECT / consequence correction (both seats, independently traced the same call chain): the title's claim that a corrupt lead_sigma key 'would abort coordinator setup' is FALSE. coordinator.py:7230 _async_load_accuracy wraps only `await self._accuracy_store.async_load()` in its try/except; AccuracyTracker.from_dict sits OUTSIDE it, and the coroutine is one of twelve fire-and-forget self._spawn(load()) background tasks (coordinator.py:672-690). An unhandled ValueError there kills that one task silently -- it does not abort setup. The real, corrected consequence: dhw_accuracy, defrost derate, peak tracker, stored mode and the comfort learner (five further learners sharing the same launch method) stay at constructor defaults on every restart, with only a task-exception log nobody reads. Fix should target from_dict's key handling AND/OR the fire-and-forget task's error handling, not an 'abort setup' framing.
notes.D3-06: Seat 2 traces the consequence further than the finder: nothing catches the ValueError between _parse_block and the coordinator's outer handler (async_refresh's own docstring promises 'Never raises' and does not honor it), so the whole coordinator cycle fails and every entity goes unavailable until the upstream API recovers. That is LOUD failure, not silent -- seat 2 uses this to argue low is still correct (the failure mode this seat weighs heaviest is silent plan corruption, and this is the opposite), not that the finding is wrong.

FIX DEFECT (seat 2, decisive): `executed_not_in_closure = 0` on 7 of 7 scripts measured -- the closure over-approximates in ONE direction only and never under-approximates, so this is CI seconds, not a gate hole; a regression cannot walk through it today. And THE PROPOSED FIX MOVES RISK IN: making the package import lazy (so closures shrink to what actually runs) would replace a guaranteed over-approximation with a RECORDED one, and a closure recorded from a run that did not take the lazy-import code path is exactly the under-approximation the current design structurally cannot produce. Register as hygiene; do not adopt the lazy-import fix without re-deriving and re-checking every closure.
notes.D3-10: MOST CONSEQUENTIAL finding in the set per seat 1. Both seat 1 (own independent mutant, thermal_model.py:547 wood-tank standby loss x25) and seat 2 (finder's own M01) reproduce rc=0 ('NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT') with the SENSITIVE wood_coil fixture moving materially (seat 1: 2111 leaves across 3 fixtures, baseline_cost -2.08%/-2.20%; seat 2: 458 leaves, baseline_cost 156.16->677.82 SEK, x4.34). Mechanism confirmed in source: env_drift.py:1021-1027 appends a may-drift hit and never folds it into `drifted`; only `drifted or stale` returns 1. All five SENSITIVE fixtures are committed may-drift in tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt under a block whose own header says it 'does not expire with the stamp' -- a standing condition, not a stale claim. FIX DEFECTS (three, load-bearing for whoever fixes this): (1) the finder's STATED PERTURBATION (remove wood_coil from SENSITIVE) does not reproduce as described -- wood_coil stays claimed in claimed_drift.txt, so main() should return 'MAY-DRIFT OUT OF SCOPE' and rc=1, not the rc=0 the finding reports; seat 2's substitute (delete the 'may-drift: wood_coil' comment line) is what actually flips rc 0->1 on the identical mutant. (2) Seat 3's harness (verify3_sensitive_projection.py / verify3_projection_clean.json) shows the finder's PROPOSED REMEDY -- judge SENSITIVE fixtures on a coarse 5%-relative-tolerance BLAS-stable projection of baseline_cost/predicted_cost/compressor_starts -- ALREADY FAILS on the clean, unmutated baseline: projection_fails=1 of 5 (wood_coil), worst_rel_gap=0.142 (14.2%) against the proposed 5% tolerance, purely from machine-to-machine BLAS variance. The proposed tolerance is too tight to ship as-is; it would false-positive on an unmodified tree. (3) Seat 2 corrects the finder's description of M01 itself: it is an operator-precedence scramble (`draw_kw * max(0.0, dhw_setpoint - t_in) / span` -> `draw_kw * dhw_setpoint - t_in / span`), not merely 'the max(0,...) clamp deleted' -- which is why one fixture moves 4.34x rather than a little. Seat 2 also narrows the blind spot honestly: 3 of the 5 SENSITIVE fixtures share every scenario switch with a judged scenario, so the true escape route is about two config switches wide (dhw_wood_coil_enabled + one topology switch), not all five fixtures independently.
